# LoadRunner Coverage

Generated evaluation of LoadRunner import coverage against the APEX Load conversion engine: Web (HTTP/HTML) functions, Java Vuser `lr` API functions, TruClient steps, and Java Vuser import surfaces.

## Web function coverage

Evaluation of the complete published OpenText/Micro Focus VuGen 26.1 **Web (HTTP/HTML)** protocol function library against the APEX Load conversion engine (`pkg/convert/enterprisearchive`). Source: VuGen Function Reference, "Alphabetical Listing of Web Functions".

**Total published functions:** 81

| Disposition | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `executable` | 46 | Translated to an executable DSL action or config mapping. |
| `native_noop` | 6 | Preserved as a runtime-compatibility attribute; a guaranteed no-op in APEX Load (no client cache / no auto-resource fetch). |
| `review_only` | 29 | Preserved in the import-review artifact; no APEX runtime equivalent, so it is not executed (never fabricated). |

Every published function resolves to one of the dispositions above — none falls through to a `custom_call` review stub. This is enforced by `TestWebHTTPFunctionRegistryResolvesEveryPublishedFunction`.

## Java LR function coverage

Evaluation of the complete published OpenText/Micro Focus VuGen 26.1 Java Vuser **lr API** (the `lrapi.lr` class) against the APEX Load conversion engine (`pkg/convert/enterprisearchive`). Source: VuGen Function Reference, "Alphabetical Listing - Java Utility Functions".

A Java Vuser script is arbitrary Java, not a closed library — so this matrix covers the **closed `lr` API** only. Java-over-HTTP, JMS, JDBC, SOAP, and no-runtime Java middleware families are reported separately by the enterprise support-matrix endpoint. Every family remains inside one combined `java_vuser` draft; these rows are review/runtime-shim dispositions, not native lane extraction. Launch requires authoring approval and an enabled governed JVM runner.

**Total tracked lr methods:** 59 (shared C `lr_*` baseline plus Java-only/alias supplement)

| Disposition | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `executable` | 22 | The persistent Java runner/shim has a meaningful runtime implementation for the call. |
| `native_noop` | 0 | The call reaches the shim but is intentionally a no-op in APEX Load; the source mapping states that explicitly. |
| `review_only` | 37 | Source and any bounded diagnostic event are preserved, but faithful LoadRunner semantics are not verified; a reachable call blocks promotion. |
| `external_required` | 0 | Needs an external provider (secret manager) before replay. |

Every published lr method resolves to one of the dispositions above — none falls through to a `custom_call` review stub. These are Java-runner dispositions, including explicit overrides where the shared native-conversion registry would overstate sidecar behavior. A reachable `review_only` call is a fidelity blocker, while an unused helper remains review evidence only.

## TruClient step coverage

Evaluation of the complete published OpenText/Micro Focus VuGen 25.1 **TruClient** step toolbox against the APEX Load conversion engine (`pkg/convert/trueclient`). Source: VuGen Function Reference, "TruClient step arguments".

Scope = the **Web + Mobile Web** step toolbox (classic TruClient and TruClient 2.0). TruClient **Native Mobile** is out of scope (external-runner, no browser DSL).

> Two-level distinction: the step matrix below is shared across TruClient variants, but **script-type executability differs** — TruClient 2.0 - Web and Mobile Web import as executable browser profiles, while classic **TruClient - Web stays review-only/planned** until it has fixture-backed replay validation. A `supported` step does not by itself make classic TruClient - Web executable. Browser VUsers remain diagnostic canaries; HTTP/API protocols carry density load after conversion.

**Total published steps:** 47

| Disposition | Count | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `supported` | 30 | Translated to an executable browser/engine DSL action. |
| `review_only` | 17 | Preserved as a review-gated placeholder; embeds arbitrary code or has no browser-replay equivalent, so it is not executed (never fabricated). |
| `planned` | 0 | Recognized; conversion path planned. |
| `out_of_scope` | 0 | Outside the browser import scope. |

Every published step resolves to one of the dispositions above — none is silently skipped. Enforced by `TestLookupStepScopeResolvesEveryPublishedStep` and `TestConvertReviewOnlyStepsPreservedNotSkipped`.

| Step | Family | Status | Target | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Activate` | switch_tab | `supported` | browser_switch_window | Activate / Activate Tab change focus via browser_switch_window. Add Tab / Close Tab also switch focus but warn that tab open/close lifecycle is not replayed (no close-window action). |
| `Activate Tab` | switch_tab | `supported` | browser_switch_window | Activate / Activate Tab change focus via browser_switch_window. Add Tab / Close Tab also switch focus but warn that tab open/close lifecycle is not replayed (no close-window action). |

| `Else` | control_if | `supported` | control_if | Recognized TruClient branch conditions map to DSL control_if blocks; unrecognized conditions preserve branch bodies behind review-gated always-true wrappers. |
| `End Transaction` | end_transaction | `supported` | transaction metadata | Transaction close events remain in scope with the same preservation model as start events. |
| `Evaluate C` | evaluate_c | `review_only` | source_review | Arbitrary C code has no browser-runtime equivalent; preserved as a review-gated placeholder and never executed. |
| `Evaluate JavaScript` | evaluate_javascript | `review_only` | browser_fill, browser_click, browser_swipe, or browser_navigate when decomposable | Simple jQuery .val(...), .attr('value', ...), .click(), and .trigger('click'), document.querySelector, first-match document.querySelectorAll, document.getElementById, first-match document.getElementsByName, first-match document.getElementsByClassName with safe class tokens, first-match document.getElementsByTagName with safe tag tokens, and document.forms[].elements[] fill/click statements plus window scroll and location navigation statements are decomposed into native browser actions. Collection first-match access supports both [0] and item(0). Statements that cannot be decomposed are imported as executable browser_evaluate_js actions but remain review-gated so recorded JavaScript is validated before promotion. |

| `Get Property` | get_property | `review_only` | source_review | Reading a DOM property into a parameter has no browser-action extractor equivalent; preserved for review. |

| `Go Forward` | go_forward | `review_only` | source_review | There is no browser history runtime; fabricating a navigate URL would be wrong, so Go Forward is preserved for review. |
| `If Block` | control_if | `supported` | control_if | Recognized TruClient branch conditions map to DSL control_if blocks; unrecognized conditions preserve branch bodies behind review-gated always-true wrappers. |

| `Mouse Over` | hover | `supported` | browser_hover | Hover and mouse-over steps map to the native browser_hover action using the captured selector or highest-confidence object-repository candidate. |

## Java Vuser import coverage

This matrix covers the Java Vuser importer surfaces outside the closed `lrapi.lr` utility API. Every Java archive remains one `java_vuser` draft so init/action/end source ordering and per-VUser Java state are preserved. Static idiom analysis supplies review evidence only; launch requires approval plus an enabled governed JVM runner advertising `java_vuser_persistent_lifecycle_v1` and `java_vuser_session_frame_token_v1`.

### Surface Disposition

| ID | Area | Construct | Status | Execution | Review | Fields | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `java-lr-api` | LoadRunner Utility API | lrapi.lr.* | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes | transaction, parameter, message, runtime, timer | The closed lr API is classified for review and transaction evidence; its source remains in the combined governed Java Vuser draft. |
| `java-vm-runtime-settings` | Java VM | default.cfg [JavaVM:Options] | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes | config.java_vuser.jdk_selection, config.java_vuser.jdk_home, config.java_vuser.additional_vm_parameters, config.java_vuser.classpath, config.java_vuser.use_xbootclasspath, config.java_vuser.dedicated_class_loader | JDK, exact JVM argument, precompiled classpath, Xboot compatibility, and dedicated-loader settings are imported with per-setting parity status and validated by the governed runner before execution. |
| `java-web-http` | HTTP | web.* / HttpURLConnection / HttpClient / Apache HttpClient | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes | url, method, headers, body, transactions | HTTP evidence is reported for review, but Java source remains in one java_vuser draft so fields and phase ordering are preserved. |
| `java-jms` | Messaging | javax.jms / jakarta.jms | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes | provider, destination, body, properties, transactions | JMS evidence is reported for review; calls remain in the same source-order-preserving Java Vuser draft as every other Java protocol family. |
| `java-jdbc` | Database | java.sql DriverManager/Connection/PreparedStatement | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes | sql, query, exec, commit, rollback | JDBC evidence is reported for review; statements are not extracted into a separate database script. |
| `java-soap` | SOAP | JAX-WS / SOAPMessage / Axis / CXF | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes | endpoint, envelope | SOAP evidence is reported for review; clients remain part of the combined Java Vuser runner draft. |
| `java-no-runtime-surfaces` | Review | RMI, EJB, CORBA, SAP GUI Java, Jacada, Oracle NCA, Tuxedo | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes |  | Middleware calls are preserved in the combined source and require the governed runner classpath to supply their dependencies. |
| `java-custom-code` | Custom Java | helpers, third-party clients, arbitrary Java | `supported` | `external_runner_required` | yes |  | Arbitrary Java is preserved in one review draft; launch requires authoring approval and an enabled governed runner. |
